title: A week in Matrix
excerpt: An experience report (read: rant) from an administrator and moderator perspective on how trying to foster an online community in the Matrix ecosystem feels like
content_html:
A Monday in Matrix

A user accidentally writes in the room of a Matrix space, resulting in every member of that space getting a notification. Matrix spaces are just regular rooms, and the fallback for old clients which don't support spaces is to render them as completely regular chat rooms. On the other side, new clients that do support spaces have very confusing UI when people start chatting in them, because that's not supposed to happen. (Yet, most clients don't adjust the room permissions in spaces to disallow people to chat in there. That would be too easy.)

I figure out how to get Element Web to display the space as a regular room in order to inspect it (it's in the devtools), give myself admin permissions and adjust the room's permissions to disallow chatting in the space room.

A Tuesday in Matrix

A user reports a spurious ban on the forum, saying they got banned from our Matrix space and have no idea why. A quick Draupnir query for the user handle shows nothing of interest. After some tring around, I query Draupnir for the domain of the user handle instead. Indeed, it finds one entry:

!foQLZposNt3iEpkl5O:example.org

  • m.policy.rule.server (m.ban): … (spam)

Apparently, someone on a moderation list our space is subscribed to banned the user's domain (it looks like it might be a single-user personal instance). I am not in the room !foQLZposNt3iEpkl5O:example.org, which I assume is the policy room from which the ban is coming, and Matrix annoyingly won't tell me its title. But it seems to be public, so I try to join it to find out. My homeserver chokes a little while trying to join me, WARN conduwuit_api::client::sync::v3::joined: timeline for newly joined room is empty, but it then asks another server to backfill the timeline, and then I only have to "clear cache and reload" my client (which will incidentally also mark all my chats as unread, which I'll have to manually clear again afterwards) and I'm in.

The room is one of those community-pooled policy rooms, full of messages of type m.policy.rule.user originating from both mods and moderation bots, which ban people and servers with sometimes very explicit usernames. I search for the domain of the affected user, but Element will only search through messages of type m.messages and thus the search comes in blank. The usual workaround for when the search doesn't work is to export the chat as HTML, then grep through it in the hope that the relevant message is in the exported range. Luckily, the room export indeed includes all message types, and grepping for the domain gives me seven hits.

It turns out, the homeserver of the affected user accidentally had had open registrations at some point in the past, with the expected consequences. Mystery solved. Getting this info took me roughly 40 minutes. It should have been two at most.

Postscriptum: Two weeks later, I get contacted by that user again, they still struggle with being banned. All I can see is that their domain is still on the ban list. I can't find an easy way of making local overrides to the ban list, so there is little we can do but to unsubscribe from the entire ban list, which would potentially expose the entire community to spam and abuse.

A Wednesday in Matrix

While onboarding a new person to our Matrix space, they don't seem to be able to see one of the rooms, despite being "suggested" for that space. After them manually joining that room, it does show up in the space's room list. The issue can be reproduced from various accounts on different homeservers.

Removing and adding the room to the space again does not seem to help. Even tombstoning and recreating the room does not seem to be a solution. However, if one of the space admins joins the room, it suddenly shows up in the space's room list again. When they leave again, the room disappears anew.

We accept the obvious workaround and move on.

A Thursday in Matrix

After some routine server maintenance, Draupnir stops responding to admin commands. According to the server logs, Draupnir seems to be processing the commands just fine. Some long debugging sessions reveal that this is an outbound federation problem with the Draupnir's homeserver (it is the only account on there). More debugging reveals that this is an issue with the Dendrite default configuration which drops all egress IPv6 traffic for no good reason.

Noticing and debugging the issue took over a month in total, during which the community space was without protection from a moderation bot. I am very glad that we were not hit by a porn&gore spam wave during that time.

Dendrite is kind of deprecated as a homeserver these days, at least it doesn't seem to be the main focus of development and most recent commits are mere dependency bumps. Years ago, when the server was set up, choosing Dendrite seemed like a good decision, because it was easier to deploy and maintain than Synapse and there was a promise for a bright future for the first 2nd generation homeserver implementation. Unfortunately, migrating between Matrix homeserver implementations remains a problem with no satisfying solution, so we're kind of stuck on slowly rotting foundations.

A Friday in Matrix

A user accidentally writes in the room of a Matrix space, resulting in every member of that space getting a notification. Again. In the same room as last time, despite me setting the permissions a couple of months ago. I go check, and the permissions have somehow reset themselves. Some testing confirms that the room seems to have desynced, because when I re-apply the permissions change they don't show up for people on other home servers, allowing them to continue chatting in the space room. The workaround is to have someone else on a different homeserver apply the changes and hope that it propagates to sufficiently many other homeservers on the other side of the desync.

A split brained Matrix room like this means that some users might be allowed to chat in that room, and those messages would propagate to other homeservers who haven't received the permissions change. However, homeservers who do would soft-fail those messages, rendering the chat invisible to the other side of the split.

The room is overdue for a room version upgrade anyways, so we end up not investigating this any further for the time being.

A Saturday in Matrix

My homeserver had degraded federation for a couple of days. The root cause isn't super important, but it was something with DNS (of course) causing server resolution to fail and resulting in the server connecting to its peers on wrong default ports, leading to directional communication breakdown. The issue once identified was quickly fixed, but unfortunately the homeserver did not properly resume operation afterwards: Unfortunately, something desynced along the way, and the server ended up thinking of one account not being in a certain room. Fortunately this was just a bot account, so kicking it from the room and re-inviting it resolved the issue. But still, I wonder: How many others users am I accidentally ghosting because my homeserver just "forgot" about them?

A Sunday in Matrix

The Matrix Foundation's Mastodon account once again boosts some toot from a person reporting a very happy experience using Matrix. The user looks like they've never joind a group chat larger than a handful of people, mostly use 1:1 DMs and don't know what spaces are. If they self-host, they likely are running a Synapse server with some Element client, but most likely they're just happily chugging along in the matrix.org silo.

I'd like to be happy for them, but I can't help not feeling somewhat gaslit by the stark contrast between the happy stories boosted into my timeline and my personal reality of helping run an actual community in this ecosystem. On a certain level this makes sense: How good a tool is heavily depends on the purpose you use it for, and Matrix undeniably does have its strengths. And the usage patterns for Matrix I find myself in clearly aren't getting as much love and dedication as others. Some are a matter of use case: Focusing on the needs of WhatsApp and Signal users first arguably makes sense. Others are a matter of principle: When the experience suffers from ecosystem software diversity due to interoperability issues, then something fundamental about the project's values is lost. Saying "Matrix is great but only if you use the flagship client on a flagship server made by the flagship company" doesn't have the same ring to it.

Some kind of clash between ideals and financial reality is inevitable to any project with ambition, but expectation management is key here. Because as of right now, the clash between PR touting "we are a serious Discord alternative" on social media all the while the development reality being "spaces are low priority, because they're a feature for more 'advanced' users" is jarring. Maybe I'd be feeling less bitter about all of this if not for all the broken promises over all these years.

sentences.en: We accept the obvious workaround and move on.

sentences.en: A Thursday in Matrix
sentences.zh: 《矩阵》中的星期四

blocks.html_en: After some routine server maintenance, Draupnir stops responding to admin commands. According to the server logs, Draupnir seems to be processing the commands just fine. Some long debugging sessions reveal that this is an outbound federation problem with the Draupnir's homeserver (it is the only account on there). More debugging reveals that this is an issue with the Dendrite default configuration which drops all egress IPv6 traffic for no good reason.

sentences.en: After some routine server maintenance, Draupnir stops responding to admin commands.
sentences.zh: 经过一些例行服务器维护后，Draupnir 停止响应管理命令。

sentences.en: According to the server logs, Draupnir seems to be processing the commands just fine.
sentences.zh: 根据服务器日志，Draupnir 似乎处理命令的情况很好。

sentences.en: Some long debugging sessions reveal that this is an outbound federation problem with the Draupnir's homeserver (it is the only account on there).
sentences.zh: 一些长时间的调试会话表明，这是 Draupnir 的主服务器（它是那里唯一的帐户）的出站联合问题。

sentences.en: More debugging reveals that this is an issue with the Dendrite default configuration which drops all egress IPv6 traffic for no good reason.
sentences.zh: 更多调试表明，这是 Dendrite 默认配置的问题，该配置会无缘无故地丢弃所有出口 IPv6 流量。

blocks.html_en: Noticing and debugging the issue took over a month in total, during which the community space was without protection from a moderation bot. I am very glad that we were not hit by a porn&gore spam wave during that time.

sentences.en: Noticing and debugging the issue took over a month in total, during which the community space was without protection from a moderation bot.
sentences.zh: 注意到并调试这个问题总共花了一个多月的时间，在此期间社区空间没有受到审核机器人的保护。

sentences.en: I am very glad that we were not hit by a porn&gore spam wave during that time.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我们在那段时间没有受到色情和血腥垃圾邮件浪潮的打击。

blocks.html_en: Dendrite is kind of deprecated as a homeserver these days, at least it doesn't seem to be the main focus of development and most recent commits are mere dependency bumps. Years ago, when the server was set up, choosing Dendrite seemed like a good decision, because it was easier to deploy and maintain than Synapse and there was a promise for a bright future for the first 2nd generation homeserver implementation. Unfortunately, migrating between Matrix homeserver implementations remains a problem with no satisfying solution, so we're kind of stuck on slowly rotting foundations.

sentences.en: Dendrite is kind of deprecated as a homeserver these days, at least it doesn't seem to be the main focus of development and most recent commits are mere dependency bumps.
sentences.zh: 如今，Dendrite 作为家庭服务器已被弃用，至少它似乎不是开发的主要焦点，而且最近的提交只是依赖项的增加。

sentences.en: Years ago, when the server was set up, choosing Dendrite seemed like a good decision, because it was easier to deploy and maintain than Synapse and there was a promise for a bright future for the first 2nd generation homeserver implementation.
sentences.zh: 几年前，当服务器建立时，选择 Dendrite 似乎是一个不错的决定，因为它比 Synapse 更容易部署和维护，并且第一个第二代家庭服务器实施有望拥有光明的未来。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, migrating between Matrix homeserver implementations remains a problem with no satisfying solution, so we're kind of stuck on slowly rotting foundations.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，Matrix 家庭服务器实现之间的迁移仍然是一个问题，没有令人满意的解决方案，因此我们有点陷入了缓慢腐烂的基础。

sentences.en: A Friday in Matrix
sentences.zh: 《黑客帝国》中的星期五

blocks.html_en: A user accidentally writes in the room of a Matrix space, resulting in every member of that space getting a notification. Again. In the same room as last time, despite me setting the permissions a couple of months ago. I go check, and the permissions have somehow reset themselves. Some testing confirms that the room seems to have desynced, because when I re-apply the permissions change they don't show up for people on other home servers, allowing them to continue chatting in the space room. The workaround is to have someone else on a different homeserver apply the changes and hope that it propagates to sufficiently many other homeservers on the other side of the desync.

sentences.en: A user accidentally writes in the room of a Matrix space, resulting in every member of that space getting a notification.
sentences.zh: 用户不小心在 Matrix 空间的房间中写入，导致该空间的每个成员都会收到通知。

sentences.en: Again.
sentences.zh: 再次。

sentences.en: In the same room as last time, despite me setting the permissions a couple of months ago.
sentences.zh: 和上次在同一个房间，尽管我几个月前设置了权限。

sentences.en: I go check, and the permissions have somehow reset themselves.
sentences.zh: 我去检查了一下，权限已经以某种方式自行重置了。

sentences.en: Some testing confirms that the room seems to have desynced, because when I re-apply the permissions change they don't show up for people on other home servers, allowing them to continue chatting in the space room.
sentences.zh: 一些测试证实房间似乎已经不同步，因为当我重新应用权限更改时，它们不会向其他家庭服务器上的人员显示，从而允许他们继续在空间房间中聊天。

sentences.en: The workaround is to have someone else on a different homeserver apply the changes and hope that it propagates to sufficiently many other homeservers on the other side of the desync.
sentences.zh: 解决方法是让不同主服务器上的其他人应用更改，并希望它传播到不同步另一端的足够多的其他主服务器。

blocks.html_en: A split brained Matrix room like this means that some users might be allowed to chat in that room, and those messages would propagate to other homeservers who haven't received the permissions change. However, homeservers who do would soft-fail those messages, rendering the chat invisible to the other side of the split.

sentences.en: A split brained Matrix room like this means that some users might be allowed to chat in that room, and those messages would propagate to other homeservers who haven't received the permissions change.
sentences.zh: 像这样的裂脑 Matrix 房间意味着某些用户可能被允许在该房间中聊天，并且这些消息将传播到尚未收到权限更改的其他家庭服务器。

sentences.en: However, homeservers who do would soft-fail those messages, rendering the chat invisible to the other side of the split.
sentences.zh: 然而，这样做的家庭服务器会对这些消息进行软失败，从而使聊天对分裂的另一方不可见。

blocks.html_en: The room is overdue for a room version upgrade anyways, so we end up not investigating this any further for the time being.

sentences.en: The room is overdue for a room version upgrade anyways, so we end up not investigating this any further for the time being.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，房间版本升级已经过期，所以我们暂时不再进一步调查此事。

sentences.en: A Saturday in Matrix
sentences.zh: 《黑客帝国》中的周六

blocks.html_en: My homeserver had degraded federation for a couple of days. The root cause isn't super important, but it was something with DNS (of course) causing server resolution to fail and resulting in the server connecting to its peers on wrong default ports, leading to directional communication breakdown. The issue once identified was quickly fixed, but unfortunately the homeserver did not properly resume operation afterwards: Unfortunately, something desynced along the way, and the server ended up thinking of one account not being in a certain room. Fortunately this was just a bot account, so kicking it from the room and re-inviting it resolved the issue. But still, I wonder: How many others users am I accidentally ghosting because my homeserver just "forgot" about them?

sentences.en: My homeserver had degraded federation for a couple of days.
sentences.zh: 我的家庭服务器几天来联盟降级了。

sentences.en: The root cause isn't super important, but it was something with DNS (of course) causing server resolution to fail and resulting in the server connecting to its peers on wrong default ports, leading to directional communication breakdown.
sentences.zh: 根本原因并不是非常重要，但它是 DNS 的问题（当然）导致服务器解析失败并导致服务器在错误的默认端口上连接到其对等方，从而导致定向通信故障。

sentences.en: The issue once identified was quickly fixed, but unfortunately the homeserver did not properly resume operation afterwards: Unfortunately, something desynced along the way, and the server ended up thinking of one account not being in a certain room.
sentences.zh: 发现的问题很快就得到了解决，但不幸的是，家庭服务器后来没有正确恢复运行：不幸的是，一路上有些东西不同步，服务器最终认为一个帐户不在某个房间中。

sentences.en: Fortunately this was just a bot account, so kicking it from the room and re-inviting it resolved the issue.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，这只是一个机器人帐户，因此将其从房间中踢出并重新邀请它可以解决问题。

sentences.en: But still, I wonder: How many others users am I accidentally ghosting because my homeserver just "forgot" about them?
sentences.zh: 但我仍然想知道：有多少其他用户因为我的家庭服务器“忘记”而意外消失了？

blocks.html_en: The Matrix Foundation's Mastodon account once again boosts some toot from a person reporting a very happy experience using Matrix. The user looks like they've never joind a group chat larger than a handful of people, mostly use 1:1 DMs and don't know what spaces are. If they self-host, they likely are running a Synapse server with some Element client, but most likely they're just happily chugging along in the matrix.org silo.

sentences.en: The Matrix Foundation's Mastodon account once again boosts some toot from a person reporting a very happy experience using Matrix.
sentences.zh: Matrix 基金会的 Mastodon 帐户再次引起了有人报告使用 Matrix 的非常愉快的体验。

sentences.en: The user looks like they've never joind a group chat larger than a handful of people, mostly use 1:1 DMs and don't know what spaces are.
sentences.zh: 用户看起来从未加入过超过少数人的群聊，大多使用 1:1 DM，并且不知道什么是空间。

sentences.en: If they self-host, they likely are running a Synapse server with some Element client, but most likely they're just happily chugging along in the matrix.org silo.
sentences.zh: 如果他们自行托管，他们很可能正在运行带有某些 Element 客户端的 Synapse 服务器，但很可能他们只是在 Matrix.org 筒仓中愉快地相处。

blocks.html_en: I'd like to be happy for them, but I can't help not feeling somewhat gaslit by the stark contrast between the happy stories boosted into my timeline and my personal reality of helping run an actual community in this ecosystem. On a certain level this makes sense: How good a tool is heavily depends on the purpose you use it for, and Matrix undeniably does have its strengths. And the usage patterns for Matrix I find myself in clearly aren't getting as much love and dedication as others. Some are a matter of use case: Focusing on the needs of WhatsApp and Signal users first arguably makes sense. Others are a matter of principle: When the experience suffers from ecosystem software diversity due to interoperability issues, then something fundamental about the project's values is lost. Saying "Matrix is great but only if you use the flagship client on a flagship server made by the flagship company" doesn't have the same ring to it.

sentences.en: I'd like to be happy for them, but I can't help not feeling somewhat gaslit by the stark contrast between the happy stories boosted into my timeline and my personal reality of helping run an actual community in this ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 我很想为他们感到高兴，但我不禁感到有点气愤，因为我的时间线中出现的快乐故事与我在这个生态系统中帮助运营一个实际社区的个人现实之间形成了鲜明的对比。

sentences.en: On a certain level this makes sense: How good a tool is heavily depends on the purpose you use it for, and Matrix undeniably does have its strengths.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这是有道理的：一个工具的好坏在很大程度上取决于你使用它的目的，而不可否认的是，Matrix 确实有它的优势。

sentences.en: And the usage patterns for Matrix I find myself in clearly aren't getting as much love and dedication as others.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己的 Matrix 使用模式显然没有像其他人那样得到那么多的爱和奉献。

sentences.en: Some are a matter of use case: Focusing on the needs of WhatsApp and Signal users first arguably makes sense.
sentences.zh: 有些是用例问题：首先关注 WhatsApp 和 Signal 用户的需求可以说是有意义的。

sentences.en: Others are a matter of principle: When the experience suffers from ecosystem software diversity due to interoperability issues, then something fundamental about the project's values is lost.
sentences.zh: 其他的是原则问题：当体验因互操作性问题而受到生态系统软件多样性的影响时，项目价值的一些基本内容就会丢失。

sentences.en: Saying "Matrix is great but only if you use the flagship client on a flagship server made by the flagship company" doesn't have the same ring to it.
sentences.zh: 说“Matrix 很棒，但前提是您在旗舰公司制造的旗舰服务器上使用旗舰客户端”并没有同样的意义。

blocks.html_en: Some kind of clash between ideals and financial reality is inevitable to any project with ambition, but expectation management is key here. Because as of right now, the clash between PR touting "we are a serious Discord alternative" on social media all the while the development reality being "spaces are low priority, because they're a feature for more 'advanced' users" is jarring. Maybe I'd be feeling less bitter about all of this if not for all the broken promises over all these years.

sentences.en: Some kind of clash between ideals and financial reality is inevitable to any project with ambition, but expectation management is key here.
sentences.zh: 对于任何雄心勃勃的项目来说，理想与财务现实之间的某种冲突是不可避免的，但期望管理是关键。

sentences.en: Because as of right now, the clash between PR touting "we are a serious Discord alternative" on social media all the while the development reality being "spaces are low priority, because they're a feature for more 'advanced' users" is jarring.
sentences.zh: 因为截至目前，公关在社交媒体上宣传“我们是一个严肃的 Discord 替代品”，而开发现实是“空间的优先级较低，因为它们是更‘高级’用户的功能”，两者之间的冲突是令人不安的。

sentences.en: Maybe I'd be feeling less bitter about all of this if not for all the broken promises over all these years.
sentences.zh: 如果不是这些年来我违背了承诺，也许我对这一切不会感到那么痛苦。

content_html_zh:
《矩阵》中的星期一

用户不小心在 Matrix 空间的房间中写入，导致该空间的每个成员都会收到通知。 矩阵空间只是普通房间，不支持空间的老客户端的后备方案是将它们呈现为完全普通的聊天室。 另一方面，当人们开始在空间中聊天时，支持空间的新客户端的用户界面会非常混乱，因为这是不应该发生的。 （然而，大多数客户不会调整空间中的房间权限以禁止人们在那里聊天。 那太容易了。）

我弄清楚如何让 Element Web 将空间显示为常规房间，以便检查它（它在开发工具中），给自己管理员权限并调整房间的权限以禁止在空间房间中聊天。

《矩阵》中的星期二

一位用户报告了论坛上的虚假禁令，称他们被禁止进入我们的 Matrix 空间，但不知道原因。 对用户句柄的快速 Draupnir 查询没有显示出任何有趣的内容。 经过一番尝试后，我改为向 Draupnir 查询用户句柄的域。 事实上，它找到了一个条目：

!foQLZposNt3iEpkl5O:example.org m.policy.rule.server (m.ban): … （垃圾邮件）

显然，我们空间的审核列表上的某个人订阅了禁止该用户的域（看起来可能是单用户个人实例）。 我不在房间 !foQLZposNt3iEpkl5O:example.org 中，我认为该房间是发出禁令的政策室，而 Matrix 烦人地不告诉我它的标题。 但它似乎是公开的，所以我尝试加入它来了解一下。 我的家庭服务器在尝试加入我时有点卡住，警告 conduwuit_api::client::sync::v3::joined: 新加入房间的时间线为空，但它随后要求另一台服务器回填时间线，然后我只需要“清除缓存并重新加载”我的客户端（这也会顺便将我的所有聊天标记为未读，之后我必须再次手动清除），然后我就加入了。

该房间是社区共享的策略室之一，充满了来自 mods 和审核机器人的 m.policy.rule.user 类型的消息，这些消息有时会禁止使用非常明确的用户名的人员和服务器。 我搜索受影响用户的域，但 Element 只会搜索 m.messages 类型的消息，因此搜索结果为空。 当搜索不起作用时，通常的解决方法是将聊天导出为 HTML，然后对其进行 grep，希望相关消息位于导出的范围内。 幸运的是，房间导出确实包括所有消息类型，并且 grep 域给了我七次点击。

事实证明，受影响用户的家庭服务器在过去的某个时刻意外地进行了开放注册，从而产生了预期的后果。 谜团解开了。 我花了大约 40 分钟才得到这些信息。 最多应该是两个。

后记：两周后，该用户再次联系我，他们仍在为被封禁而苦苦挣扎。 我只能看到他们的域名仍然在禁止列表中。 我找不到一种简单的方法来对禁止列表进行本地覆盖，因此我们只能取消整个禁止列表的订阅，这可能会使整个社区面临垃圾邮件和滥用行为。

《黑客帝国》中的星期三

当新人加入我们的 Matrix 空间时，他们似乎无法看到其中一个房间，尽管他们被“建议”进入该空间。 在他们手动加入该房间后，它确实会显示在该空间的房间列表中。 可以从不同家庭服务器上的不同帐户重现该问题。

再次删除房间并将其添加到空间中似乎没有帮助。 即使是墓碑和重建房间似乎也不是解决方案。 但是，如果其中一位空间管理员加入该房间，它会突然再次出现在该空间的房间列表中。 当他们再次离开时，房间又重新消失了。

我们接受明显的解决方法并继续前进。

《矩阵》中的星期四

经过一些例行服务器维护后，Draupnir 停止响应管理命令。 根据服务器日志，Draupnir 似乎处理命令的情况很好。 一些长时间的调试会话表明，这是 Draupnir 的主服务器（它是那里唯一的帐户）的出站联合问题。 更多调试表明，这是 Dendrite 默认配置的问题，该配置会无缘无故地丢弃所有出口 IPv6 流量。

注意到并调试这个问题总共花了一个多月的时间，在此期间社区空间没有受到审核机器人的保护。 我很高兴我们在那段时间没有受到色情和血腥垃圾邮件浪潮的打击。

如今，Dendrite 作为家庭服务器已被弃用，至少它似乎不是开发的主要焦点，而且最近的提交只是依赖项的增加。 几年前，当服务器建立时，选择 Dendrite 似乎是一个不错的决定，因为它比 Synapse 更容易部署和维护，并且第一个第二代家庭服务器实施有望拥有光明的未来。 不幸的是，Matrix 家庭服务器实现之间的迁移仍然是一个问题，没有令人满意的解决方案，因此我们有点陷入了缓慢腐烂的基础。

《黑客帝国》中的星期五

用户不小心在 Matrix 空间的房间中写入，导致该空间的每个成员都会收到通知。 再次。 和上次在同一个房间，尽管我几个月前设置了权限。 我去检查了一下，权限已经以某种方式自行重置了。 一些测试证实房间似乎已经不同步，因为当我重新应用权限更改时，它们不会向其他家庭服务器上的人员显示，从而允许他们继续在空间房间中聊天。 解决方法是让不同主服务器上的其他人应用更改，并希望它传播到不同步另一端的足够多的其他主服务器。

像这样的裂脑 Matrix 房间意味着某些用户可能被允许在该房间中聊天，并且这些消息将传播到尚未收到权限更改的其他家庭服务器。 然而，这样做的家庭服务器会对这些消息进行软失败，从而使聊天对分裂的另一方不可见。

无论如何，房间版本升级已经过期，所以我们暂时不再进一步调查此事。

《黑客帝国》中的周六

我的家庭服务器几天来联盟降级了。 根本原因并不是非常重要，但它是 DNS 的问题（当然）导致服务器解析失败并导致服务器在错误的默认端口上连接到其对等方，从而导致定向通信故障。 发现的问题很快就得到了解决，但不幸的是，家庭服务器后来没有正确恢复运行：不幸的是，一路上有些东西不同步，服务器最终认为一个帐户不在某个房间中。 幸运的是，这只是一个机器人帐户，因此将其从房间中踢出并重新邀请它可以解决问题。 但我仍然想知道：有多少其他用户因为我的家庭服务器“忘记”而意外消失了？

《矩阵》中的周日

Matrix 基金会的 Mastodon 帐户再次引起了有人报告使用 Matrix 的非常愉快的体验。 用户看起来从未加入过超过少数人的群聊，大多使用 1:1 DM，并且不知道什么是空间。 如果他们自行托管，他们很可能正在运行带有某些 Element 客户端的 Synapse 服务器，但很可能他们只是在 Matrix.org 筒仓中愉快地相处。

我很想为他们感到高兴，但我不禁感到有点气愤，因为我的时间线中出现的快乐故事与我在这个生态系统中帮助运营一个实际社区的个人现实之间形成了鲜明的对比。 在某种程度上，这是有道理的：一个工具的好坏在很大程度上取决于你使用它的目的，而不可否认的是，Matrix 确实有它的优势。 我发现自己的 Matrix 使用模式显然没有像其他人那样得到那么多的爱和奉献。 有些是用例问题：首先关注 WhatsApp 和 Signal 用户的需求可以说是有意义的。 其他的是原则问题：当体验因互操作性问题而受到生态系统软件多样性的影响时，项目价值的一些基本内容就会丢失。 说“Matrix 很棒，但前提是您在旗舰公司制造的旗舰服务器上使用旗舰客户端”并没有同样的意义。

对于任何雄心勃勃的项目来说，理想与财务现实之间的某种冲突是不可避免的，但期望管理是关键。 因为截至目前，公关在社交媒体上宣传“我们是一个严肃的 Discord 替代品”，而开发现实是“空间的优先级较低，因为它们是更‘高级’用户的功能”，两者之间的冲突是令人不安的。 如果不是这些年来我违背了承诺，也许我对这一切不会感到那么痛苦。
